images.note: Real screen capture — a report parameter prompt populated from a dataset query (the tutorial's Store name dropdown, fed by a Stores dataset) instead of a typed-in list. Same mechanism this lesson's @TerritoryGroup parameter uses, even though the tutorial's own sample filters by store, not territory. learn.microsoft.com's dedicated parameters reference page has no comparable live-dropdown screenshot, so sourced from the parameter tutorial instead.

Real screen capture — where a report parameter lands once created: the Parameters node in the Report Data pane (left) and the Parameters pane on the design surface (right). Directly shows the two places @TerritoryGroup and @CalendarYear will both appear after this lesson creates them. Image has Microsoft's own native red call-out boxes baked in around both panes — unaltered, not an added annotation.

Real screen capture — a finished Report Builder matrix with nested row groups (Territory, Sales Date) and adjacent column groups (Subcategory, then a weekday group), currency-formatted and totaled. Same grouped-matrix shape as this lesson's RegionalSalesSummary matrix (territory rows x year columns), just with the matrix tutorial's own subcategory/weekday fields instead of territory/year — used to illustrate the row+column group mechanic, not as a literal capture of this lesson's own report. Image has Microsoft's own native magenta call-out box baked in around the adjacent weekday column group — unaltered, not an added annotation.

Real screen capture — a single matrix cell selected (handles visible around it), as opposed to a row or column header. Illustrates exactly what 'select the matrix's data cell' means before opening its Action properties to wire the drillthrough in this lesson.
